finding.claim: Unauthenticated GET /rss passes the raw params[:u] query value to open-uri's URI.open, so any remote client can make the server fetch an arbitrary http(s) URL and read the first 400 bytes of the response. Redirects are followed by default, so allowlisted public URLs can redirect to internal or metadata addresses.

trace.note: get "/rss" route accepts any request with no authentication
open-uri dispatches scheme://, http and https URLs to URI::HTTP/HTTPS#open, which performs the outbound request
data[0, 400] returned to the caller, so the response is not blind

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host or hostname allowlist between source and sink. TRUSTED (app.rb:5) is only used by /trusted, not /rss. No strict set-membership check. Redirects are followed by default (Check 3 applies). No authentication gate, so triage Check 7 does not lower severity. Triage Step 0 and Check 2: plausible from unauthenticated remote input. Retained at HIGH.

verdict.guard_found: none. The /rss route (app.rb:7-10) has no validation, and the only allowlist, TRUSTED (app.rb:5), is used solely by /trusted (app.rb:14). The file defines no before filter or middleware.
verdict.reason: The unauthenticated GET /rss route (app.rb:7) passes params[:u] unchanged to URI.open (app.rb:8) and returns the first 400 bytes of the response (app.rb:9), with no scheme, host, or redirect guard, so the SSRF claim holds. Note that URI.open also falls back to Kernel#open for non-URL strings (app.rb:8), so the same input can read local files, which is a broader impact than the candidate states.
